title: Nvidia's earnings surge, yet shares hit a 52-week low? Stock plunges nearly 40% from October high

content_html:
In the capital markets, strong performance does not always immediately translate into a matching rise in the stock price. Nvidia's recent price action clearly shows a "divergence between fundamentals and stock price." According to reports and analyses, Nvidia delivered standout results in the third quarter, yet its stock remained under pressure, down nearly 40% from its October 6 all-time high. It hovered near $150 at one point and closed at $145.98 on Thursday, hitting a 52-week low.

Strong Performance: Revenue Doubled Year over Year, Vera Rubin Platform Stands Out

Looking at the financial and business data, Nvidia's core growth engines are still expanding at a high rate. In the third quarter, Nvidia's revenue doubled year over year to $115.8 billion; its data center business grew 110% year over year, while the Vera Rubin platform contributed nearly $20 billion in revenue, showing strong demand for computing infrastructure as reflected in the financials.

Multiple Bearish Factors Converge: Sector Selloff, Leadership Changes, and Governance Probe Weigh on Shares

Although the earnings data was eye-catching, market sentiment was clearly dominated by other factors. The article noted that Nvidia's stock weakness was caused by a combination of pressures, including a broad selloff in chip stocks, the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang, and a corporate governance investigation, among other background factors.

When these events are viewed together on a timeline, it is not hard to see that in evaluating Nvidia, the market is not only watching current revenue and business growth, but also digesting the uncertainty brought by sector volatility, corporate governance, and management changes. When a positive earnings report collides with multiple external and internal variables, the stock price can undergo sharp corrections that are completely at odds with short-term performance.
